public_rationale: Epoch AI measured the gap between the best open-weight and closed models from January 1 to May 28, 2026. It found an average lag of four months on its aggregate capability index, or six months under a stricter test. Both fit Marcus's 'only a few months behind'. Epoch cautions that the true gap may be somewhat larger, because open models can do worse on private benchmarks and labs may hold back their best closed models.
limitations: One measurement organization and one index.
Epoch flags possible understatement of the gap.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Open-source models, perhaps excluding Meta's, are only a few months behind frontier models.

statement.excerpt: Opensource models (though perhaps not Meta’s) are only a few months behind.
statement.document_title: Breaking news, and how the end might begin

our_interpretation: Read as: the best open-weight models trail the best closed frontier models by a few months of capability, as of the post.
'A few months' read plainly as roughly 2 to 6 months.
Period: the most recent window public measurement covered before the post, January 2026 to June 10, 2026.
The Meta caveat excludes Meta's models from the claim. The best open model in that window need not be Meta's.
criteria.support_condition: A credible measurement around the post date showing the leading open-weight models lag the closed frontier by about 2 to 6 months.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A credible measurement showing the lag is a year or more, or that open models lead.

evidence.excerpt: Since January 2026, the most capable open-weight models have lagged frontier closed models by an average of four months in the Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI), our aggregate measure of model capability.
evidence.explanation: An average four-month lag over Jan to May 2026 fits 'only a few months behind'.

evidence.excerpt: We find an average time gap of four months. This estimate would grow to six months if we required that the open-weight model’s point estimate for ECI be strictly higher
evidence.explanation: Even under the stricter test the lag is six months, still within a plain reading of 'a few months'.
